intro: Every day has an order. You wake up, you eat, you go to school, you play and you sleep. In this unit you learn to tell that order in Spanish with small signpost words: primero (first), luego (then), después (after that) and finalmente (finally).

You also learn to name the parts of the day, the days of the week and the time on the hour, like Es la una and Son las tres. You use everyday verbs such as como (I eat), voy (I go), juego (I play) and leo (I read).

Then you become a writer. You join ideas with y, pero and también. You build a short story with a beginning, a middle and an end, or draw it as a comic strip. Finally, you check your verbs and describing words and read your story aloud.
bigQuestion: How do we tell a day or a story in Spanish so that a listener can follow every step?

timeline.t: Antonio de Nebrija publishes the first grammar of the Castilian Spanish language
Juan Ponce de León founds an early Spanish settlement in Puerto Rico
Miguel de Cervantes publishes the first part of Don Quijote, a famous story told in Spanish
The Real Academia Española (RAE) is founded in Madrid to care for the Spanish language
Puerto Rico becomes a territory of the United States after the Spanish-American War
The Jones Act makes people born in Puerto Rico United States citizens
Chilean poet Gabriela Mistral wins the Nobel Prize in Literature
Puerto Rico adopts its own constitution as a commonwealth of the United States
The United States begins National Hispanic Heritage Week
Hispanic Heritage Week grows into a full month, from September 15 to October 15

words.d: first — starts the first step: Primero, desayuno
then, later — starts a next step: Luego, voy a la escuela
after that — adds a later step; note the accent on the last e
finally — marks the last step: Finalmente, duermo
the morning — without la, mañana means tomorrow
the night — Leo por la noche (I read at night)
Monday, or on Monday — days are written with small letters
What time is it? — answer Es la una or Son las dos, tres…
and — joins words or ideas: Como arroz y frijoles
but — joins ideas that differ; not the same as perro (dog)
also, too — adds a matching idea: Yo también (Me too)
the story — a short story has a beginning, a middle and an end

test.q: Which order word starts the last step?
test.why: Finalmente means finally, so it marks the last step.
Primero means first, and desayuno means I eat breakfast.

test.q: How do you say "in the afternoon"?
test.why: Spanish says por la tarde, and tarde is feminine, so it takes la.

test.q: Which day comes right after viernes?
test.why: The order is jueves, viernes, sábado. Sábado (Saturday) follows viernes.

test.q: Which sentence is correct for "On Tuesday, I read"?
test.why: Use el with the day, a small letter and leo for I read.

test.q: It is 1:00. What do you say?
test.why: One is singular, so es la una.

test.q: It is 4:00. What do you say?
test.why: Four is plural, so son las cuatro.

test.q: Which is the right form for "I play"?
test.why: Jugar changes u to ue, so I play is juego.

test.q: What does "Voy a la escuela a las ocho" mean?
choices: It is eight o'clock at school.
I eat at school at eight.
I go to school at eight o'clock.
test.why: Voy means I go, and a las ocho means at eight o'clock.

test.q: Pick the best joining word: "Me gusta el bus, ___ estoy cansado."
test.why: The second idea goes a different way, so pero (but) fits.

test.q: Which word means dog, not but?
test.why: Perro with rr means dog. Pero with one r means but.

test.q: Which is correct for "the red books"?
test.why: Libros is masculine plural, so los and rojos match it, after the noun.

test.q: Fix the verb: "Mi hermano ___ un libro."
test.why: Mi hermano is él, so leer becomes lee.

test.q: Which part of a story has the problem?
test.why: The middle tells what goes wrong. The end tells how it turns out.

test.q: Which comic bubble is punctuated correctly?
test.why: Spanish exclamations open with ¡ and close with !.

write.prompt: Escribe un cuento corto: Mi día. Write 4 to 6 Spanish sentences about one day. Tell what you do in order with primero, luego, después and finalmente. Include one time (Es la una or a las tres) and join two ideas with y, pero or también.
tips: Use the order words from this unit: primero, luego, después, finalmente.
Check every verb ending: -o for yo (como, leo, juego).
Check el and la and make describing words match: la mochila roja.
Write days with small letters and put ¿ or ¡ at the start of questions and exclamations.
Read your story aloud and join choppy sentences with y, pero or también.
